objects.definition:
enum swGlobalHookType {
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_SERVER_START,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_CLIENT_START,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_WORKER_START,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_ON_CORO_START,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_ON_CORO_STOP,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_ON_REACTOR_CREATE,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_SERVER_SHUTDOWN,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_AFTER_SERVER_SHUTDOWN,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_WORKER_STOP,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_ON_REACTOR_DESTROY,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_SERVER_CREATE,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_AFTER_SERVER_CREATE,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_AFTER_FORK,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_USER = 24,
    SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_END = SW_MAX_HOOK_TYPE - 1,
};
objects.description: Enumeration of global hook points within Swoole’s lifecycle (server/client start/stop, worker, coroutine, reactor, etc.). Values mark insertion points for user callbacks registered via swoole_add_hook. Note that SW_MAX_HOOK_TYPE is referenced but not defined in this header; its value is expected from included headers. SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_USER provides a user-reserved starting index; SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_END is the last valid hook type.

Function pointer type for hook callbacks invoked at swGlobalHookType points. The callback receives a single void* argument whose concrete type depends on the specific hook. Lifecycle and ownership of the data pointer are determined by the hook site and are not specified in this header.

functions.name: swoole_add_hook
functions.signature: void swoole_add_hook(swGlobalHookType type, swHookFunc cb, int push_back);
functions.description: Registers a global hook (callback) for a given Swoole lifecycle/event type. The callback has the signature void (*)(void *), and will be invoked later (typically via swoole_call_hook) with a user-supplied data pointer. The push_back flag controls insertion order in the internal hook list (non-zero to append; zero to prepend). Use this to attach code that should run before/after server/client/coroutine/reactor lifecycle points listed in swGlobalHookType.
requirements: type must be a valid value of swGlobalHookType (e.g., SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_BEFORE_SERVER_START, SW_GLOBAL_HOOK_ON_CORO_START, etc.).
cb must be a valid, non-null function pointer of type void (*)(void *).
push_back is treated as a boolean flag; use 0 (prepend) or non-zero (append) to control where the hook is inserted.
The callback must be able to accept a void* argument (possibly NULL) passed later by the caller of swoole_call_hook; the interpretation of this pointer is up to the callback and caller.
Ordering and thread-safety/async-signal-safety are not documented; callers should not assume concurrent safety unless guaranteed elsewhere.

functions.name: swoole_call_hook
functions.description: Invokes all callbacks registered for the specified global hook type, passing arg to each callback. Typically used internally or by integrations to trigger the registered lifecycle/event handlers.
requirements: type must be a valid value of swGlobalHookType for which hooks may have been registered.
arg is passed verbatim to each registered hook callback; it must be a pointer value that each callback can safely interpret for this hook type, or NULL if callbacks expect no data.
The memory pointed to by arg (if non-NULL) must remain valid for the duration of all callback invocations.
Reentrancy, ordering, and concurrency guarantees are not documented; callers should not assume specific ordering beyond the push_back semantics indicated when registering.

functions.name: swoole_isset_hook
functions.description: Checks whether any callback has been registered for the specified global hook type. Useful to avoid work if no hooks are present or to conditionally trigger hook execution.
requirements: type must be a valid value of swGlobalHookType.

functions.name: swoole_version
functions.description: Returns the Swoole library version string for the linked library (e.g., "x.y.z"). Intended for display, logging, or compatibility checks.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to a null-terminated string managed by the library; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: swoole_version_id
functions.description: Returns the numeric Swoole version identifier for the linked library. Typically encodes the major/minor/patch as an integer for numeric comparisons.
requirements: No arguments required; returned value is an integer suitable for comparisons against known version IDs.

functions.name: swoole_api_version_id
functions.description: Returns the numeric Swoole C API version identifier. Useful for determining API compatibility at compile-time or run-time.
requirements: No arguments required; returned value is an integer representing the API version for compatibility checks.
